scenario.name: CERT-UA #4435, ESET & CISA ICS — Industroyer2 IEC 60870-5-104 Substation Telecontrol & Protection Relay Forensics
scenario.overview: Picture a fenced municipal power substation and waterworks yard lined with tall ceramic insulator towers, heavy steel water pipes, red manual valve wheels, and a glass control room. Breaching the fenced perimeter of the municipal power substation, an impostor connects a handheld controller straight into the yard’s switchboard cabinet. In this real-world scenario, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the power substation later, then smuggles copied records out past the substation fenced entry gate in tiny disguised batches. The grid shift engineer notices the physical breaker clank outside disagrees with the frozen green gauge on the desk and pulls the mechanical override. In this scenario (T1489, CERT-UA #4435, ESET & CISA ICS, Industroyer2 IEC 60870-5-104 Substation Telecontrol & Protection Relay Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: legitimate SCADA Service Termination Prior, then iEC 60870-5-104 STARTDT_ACT Handshake, then aSDU Type 46 IOA Telecontrol Frame Audit. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Legitimate SCADA Service Termination Prior, then IEC 60870-5-104 STARTDT_ACT Handshake, then ASDU Type 46 IOA Telecontrol Frame Audit, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 3: ASDU Type 46 (C_DC_NA_1 Double Command) IOA Telecontrol Frame Audit
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1565.002 - Transmitted Data Manipulation / IEC-104 Telecontrol)
stages.description: Even as lights flicker across the district and pressure climbs inside the pipes, a falsified dial inside the glass control room keeps displaying steady green readings. In this final step inside the power substation, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the substation fenced entry gate in tiny disguised batches until the control room gauge recorder catches the mismatch. After receiving STARTDT_CON, the binary iterates through its configured Information Object Addresses (IOAs) and transmits ASDU Type 45 (C_SC_NA_1 Single Command) and Type 46 (C_DC_NA_1 Double Command) frames with Cause of Transmission = 6 (Activation) to toggle telecontrol state points (logged in IDS Alert Event 46 with AsduTypeId=46 , C_DC_NA_1, Double Command, CauseOfTransmission=6 , Activation, InformationObjectAddress=COA=12, IOA=1104 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes tshark -r substation.pcap -Y "iec60870_asdu.typeid == 45 || iec60870_asdu.typeid == 46" -T fields -e iec60870_asdu.ca -e iec60870_asdu.ioa (which Captures or inspects industrial control system , ICS/OT protocol frames and engineering workstation logs , tshark -r substation.pcap -Y "iec60870_a so that reconstructs PLC logic transfers, substation breaker telecontrol commands, or Safety Instrumented System , SIS controller state changes , T1565.002 during "ASDU Type 46 , C_DC_NA_1 Double Command IOA Telecontrol Frame Audit"). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ IEC-104 ASDU Type 46 (C_DC_NA_1 Double Command) COA=12 IOA=1104COT=6 (Activation) / ⇠#3 ALERT 46) from Node ③ (#3 Substation Gateway (:2404)) to Node ④ (#4 Substation RTU & Bay Controller), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 PServiceControl Legitimate Service).
